svg.title: States & density
svg.desc: Three states: Solid: close, fixed arrangement; vibration. Liquid: close, irregular, able to flow. Gas: widely spaced, random motion; easily compressed. Individual particles do not expand when heated. Physical changes: Melting/freezing; boiling or evaporation/condensation; sublimation solid → gas. No new substance; reversing restores properties. Open-container mass loss may be escaping vapour. Regular & irregular solids: Weigh solid. Cuboid volume = lwh; cylinder = πr²h. Use ruler, callipers or micrometer. Irregular: fully submerge; final water volume − initial = solid volume. Displacement can is an alternative. Liquids & good readings: Weigh empty dry cylinder, then cylinder + liquid. Subtract to find liquid mass. Read meniscus at eye level. Avoid bubbles/splashes; unsuitable for solids that dissolve or absorb water. Density equation: ρ = m/V; m = ρV; V = m/ρ. 240 g / 80 cm³ = 3.0 g/cm³ = 3,000 kg/m³. 1 cm³ = 10⁻⁶ m³. Keep units consistent. Explain changes: Fixed mass spreads over larger volume → lower density. Gas spacing explains low density. Do not claim every solid is denser than its liquid: ice is an exception. Repeats assess random variation; check zero errors.
